title: Loop Machines
tagline: You get the computer to repeat a job for you, and you draw with it.
objectives: I can write a loop with for and range.
I can use i inside the loop.
I can name a loop bug when I see one.
_provenance: Loop Machines, story THE SEARCH (J2_L5_SEARCH_SPEC.md, design passed 14 Oct 2026; the hour is L5_PROTOTYPES/hour with the build's listed edits, DFM 334 / K83). Written by KS3 DT Platform/L5_SEARCH_BUILD/write_j2_05.js.

ch1.h1: Type forward(10) to fly BEEP to the first hoof-print.
tour: This is the box you type in.
This card shows the line to type.
BEEP will fly along these hoof-prints.
ch1.keepGoing: The snow is filling the prints from the top. Keep going.

j.fwdOk: BEEP flew 10 metres to print {n} of 20.
j.lookOk: The torch is on. Print {n} of 20 is lit.
j.capF: Python needs the word "forward" to be in small letters.
j.noBr: forward needs brackets round its number: forward(10)
j.noClose: The line needs a closing bracket at the end.
j.noNum: forward needs a number in its brackets: forward(10)
j.lookNoBr: look needs its brackets, with nothing inside: look()
j.lookArg: look takes nothing in its brackets: look()
j.lookTwice: The torch is on at a print that is already lit. Fly forward first.
j.fwdTwice: Print {n} is not lit yet. Type look() before you fly on.
j.fwdN: forward({n}) misses the next print. Each print is 10 metres on, so type forward(10).
j.capL: Python needs the word "look" to be in small letters.

ch1.h2: Fly and light every hoof-print. Type two lines for each one.
ch1.gauge: Time until the snow buries the trail
fail: The snow has buried the trail. I am winding time back.
You typed the same two lines for every print. The snow was faster.
fast: You typed all 40 lines in time. The trail is lit.
If you had typed more slowly, the snow would have buried the trail.
ch1.holdDark: The snow waits while I show you this.
lesson: Look at this. You needed forward(10) and then look(), again and again, twenty times.
I can do the same thing again and again. Repeating is my job.
This one line tells me how many times: for i in range(20):
The letter i is the name of the loop's count. It counts each time round. You will use i in chapter 3, The spiral.
Your two lines go under the for line. Push them in by four spaces.
I repeat the pushed-in lines 20 times.
You need only three lines, not forty. Type them and watch me go.
ch1.h4: Type these 3 lines. Where you see 4 dots, type 4 spaces instead.

j4.forOk: range({w}) means {w} times. The colon says more lines come next.
j4.forNoBr: range needs brackets round its number: range({w})
j4.forN: range({n}) would fly {n} prints. There are 20 prints, so type range(20).
j4.forNoI: The letter i is missing. Type i after the word for. The whole line is: for i in range({w}):
j4.fwdIn: This line is pushed in, so it is inside the loop.
j4.fwdNoIndent: Put 4 spaces before forward, so it is inside the loop. Press the Tab key to make them.
j4.lookIn: look is inside the loop too. Both lines will fly 20 times.
j4.lookNoIndent: Put 4 spaces before look, so it is inside the loop too.
j4.forNoNum: range needs a number in its brackets: range({w})

ch1.flyIt: Press Fly it. I will do the rest.
ch1.held: You typed 3 lines. BEEP did 40 things.

close.h: A loop repeats the pushed-in lines for you.
under: Typing every line yourself would take 40 lines. The loop took 3 lines.
BEEP flew the same two lines 20 times.

close.h: These 3 lines are called a for loop.
labels: This line is pushed in, so it is inside the loop.
This line is pushed in too, so it repeats.
close.box: The pushed-in lines run once each time round the loop. range(20) means the loop goes round 20 times.

close.seen: You saw this: range(20) flew the two lines 20 times.
close.q: A new field has 12 hoof-prints. Which line flies BEEP to all of them?
opts: Yes. range(12) runs the pushed-in lines 12 times.
That would fly BEEP to 20 prints. The new field has 12.
That flies 12 metres once. A loop needs for and range.

j.short1: I flew {k} times. Count the walls.
j.over: That is {k} flights for {w} walls. That is too many. Type the number of walls in the brackets.
j.noNum: range needs a number in its brackets. Count the walls.
j.wrongTurn: The sign says left({a}). Use the turn on the sign.
j.wrongLen: Each wall is 100 metres. Use forward(100).
j.noTurn: Your loop has no turn. The sign says left({a}). Add it as a pushed-in line.

fail: It is too dark to see the walls. I am winding time back.

close.h: The number in the brackets is how many times the loop runs.
under: You counted 4, 6 and 3 walls. The loop flew 4 times, then 6 times, then 3 times.

close.h: A loop that runs one time too few has a name: off by one.
labels: {k} flights for {w} walls. One wall stayed dark.
close.box: Off by one means the number was one too small or one too big. Then the loop runs one time too few or one time too many.

close.q: A field has 5 walls. Which line lights them all?
opts: That is one too few. One wall stays dark. This bug is called off by one.
That is one too many. BEEP flies the first wall twice.

film: Beyond the top wall the field is open, and her bleat is fading.
I cannot search a whole field one wall at a time.
Watch me count. Then make my flight grow.
ch3.h1: Type these 2 lines. Each time round, BEEP will say the number in i.

j1.forOk: The loop goes round 3 times. Now type the pushed-in line.
j1.sayOk: say(i) says the count. Press Fly it.
j1.say3: say(3) says 3 every time round. Type say(i), so it says the count.
j1.sayNoBr: say needs brackets round the i: say(i)
j1.sayNoIndent: Put 4 spaces before say, so it is inside the loop.
j1.forN: The card says range({w}). Type that first.
j1.changeOk: range(5) means 5 times. Press Fly it.

ch3.held1: BEEP said 0, 1, 2. The count starts at 0.
ch3.change: Change the 3 to 5 and press Fly it again.
ch3.held2: range(5) gave 5 counts: 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4. BEEP never says 5.
ch3.h2: Fly a spiral that grows bigger. Use i in the forward line, so each flight is longer than the last.
ch3.gauge: Time left before her bleat fades

j2.found10i: 10 * i is the same as i * 10. You found her!
j2.fwd10: forward(10) flies 10 metres every time round, so the spiral never grows. Put i in the brackets.
j2.fwdI: forward(i) grows by only 1 metre each time round. This is too slow. Try forward(i * 10).
j2.shortRange: Going round {k} times only reached {m} metres. She is further out. Use range(10).
j2.longRange: You found her when i was 9. After that, the loop went round {k} more times. Use range(10) to stop there.
j2.noTurn: Your loop has no turn, so it is not a spiral. Add left(90).
j2.right90: right(90) spirals the other way round. You found her!

ch3.help1: i is 0, then 1, then 2. i * 10 is 0, 10, 20.
fail: Her bleat has faded away. I am winding time back.
Try again from the middle of the field.
ch3.held3: When i was 0, BEEP flew 0 metres. When i was 9, BEEP flew 90 metres.

close.h: i is the count. It starts at 0 and changes every time round.
under: The loop went round ten times. i went from 0 to 9. The flight grew with it.

close.h: You used the count inside the loop.
labels: The loop goes round 10 times. i goes 0, 1, 2, up to 9.
i * 10 is 0, then 10, then 20, then 90 at the end.
A quarter turn each time round makes the spiral.
close.box: i is a variable, a box with a name on it. The loop puts a new number in it each time round.

close.q: BEEP runs a loop with two lines. The first line is for i in range(4): The second line is say(i). What does BEEP say?
opts: Yes. There are four counts, and they start at 0.
range(4) is four counts, so it stops after 3.

close.h: A loop bug has a name.
under: Off by one means the count is 5 but there are 6 gates. Wrong turn means you turned 80 instead of 90. Never stops means while True has no end.

close.h: Read the loop before you run it.
labels: Off by one. The count is one short, or one over.
Wrong turn. The turn does not match the shape.
Never stops. The loop has no count, so it has no end.
close.box: Before you press Run, check three things. Check the count. Check the turn. Check that the loop has an end.

close.q: This loop should light 10 gates: for i in range(9). What is the bug?
opts: Yes. The loop goes round 9 times, but there are 10 gates.
There is no turn in this loop.

barn: The lamb is in the barn, and her mother is with her.
Nuala: Thank you. Thank you. Thank you.

recap: A loop runs its pushed-in lines once each time round. range sets how many.
The number in the brackets sets how many times the loop runs. If it is one too small, the bug is called off by one.
i is the count. It starts at 0 and changes every time round. The loop can use it.
A loop bug has a name: off by one, wrong turn, never stops.
